He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==High school career== Wigginton's mother grew up in Halifax's [[Uniacke Square]] and his father is from [[North Preston]].{{cite web |last1=Ballers |first1=Canadian |title=2017 Lindell Wigginton Suiting Up With Stackhouse Elite UPLAY |url=https://www.canadianballers.com/news_article/show/499319 |website=Canadian Ballers |language=en-us |date=4 April 2015 }}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}{{cite web |last1=Palmeter |first1=Paul |title=Nova Scotia's Lindell Wigginton contemplating early jump to NBA Social Sharing |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/nova-scotia/lindell-wigginton-contemplating-early-jump-to-nba-1.4585687 |website=CBC News |accessdate=5 April 2019}} He played one year at [[Prince Andrew High School]] in his native [[Dartmouth, Nova Scotia]] for Coach Ken Cooper {{Cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/nova-scotia/wigginton-basketball-nova-scotian-nba-1.4029150|title=Wigginton gets closer to dream of being 1st Nova Scotian to play in NBA|work=CBC News|access-date=2017-07-10|language=en}} before moving to the United States to join [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]] at the age of 15.{{Cite news|url=http://www.capebretonpost.com/sports/2017/1/17/wigginton-shining-as-first-canadian-to-play-for-storied-oak-hill-academy.html|title=Wigginton shining as first Canadian to play for storied Oak Hill Academy|work=Cape Breton Post|access-date=2017-07-10|language=en}} A four-star recruit in [[ESPN]]'s ranking,{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/204112/lindell-wigginton|title=Lindell Wigginton - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-07-10}} he committed to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] in October 2016,{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/17848883/lindell-wigginton-no-49-espn-100-commits-iowa-state-cyclones|title=Wigginton, No. 49 in ESPN 100, picks Iowa State|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-07-10}} choosing the Cyclones over schools such as [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].{{Cite web|url=http://northpolehoops.com/2016/10/21/lindell-wigginton-commits-to-iowa-state-cyclones-re-up-on-canadian-talent/|title=Lindell Wigginton Commits to Iowa State, Cyclones Re-Up on Canadian Talent|date=2016-10-21|website=Northpolehoops.com|access-date=2017-07-10}} Representing the World Select Team, Wigginton saw 22:16 minutes of action at the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], scoring eleven points and handing out a team-high seven assists.{{Cite ==College career== [[File:Lindell Wigginton.jpg|thumb|left|Wigginton with Iowa State]] As a freshman, Wigginton was one of the best players for Iowa State, averaging 16.7 points, 3.7 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game. However, he struggled with turnover problems, losing possession 92 times on the year.{{cite news |last1=Birch |first1=Tommy |title=Iowa State observations: Lindell Wigginton expecting even bigger things out of sophomore season |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/2018/10/11/cyclones-basketball-lindell-wigginton-2018-expectations-iowa-state-media-day-injuries-steve-prohm/1558085002/ |accessdate=21 October 2018 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=11 October 2018}} After the season, Wigginton declared himself eligible for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent and ultimately returned to school.{{cite news|last1=Givony|first1=Jonathan|title=Lindell Wigginton to test draft, won't hire agent, says father|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22850689/lindell-wigginton-iowa-state-cyclones-test-nba-draft-waters|accessdate=1 April 2018|work=ESPN|date=20 March 2018}} In his sophomore season, he averaged 13.4 points, four rebounds and 2.1 assists in 26 minutes per game and was named the [[Big 12 Conference]] Sixth Man of the Year. He started the first game of the season before suffering a foot injury, eventually starting two of 26 games.{{cite news |last1=Halsted |first1=Alex |title=Lindell Wigginton leaving Iowa State for NBA |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa-state/Article/Lindell-Wigginton-NBA-Draft-decision-Iowa-State-basketball-130883130/ |accessdate=8 January 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=3 April 2019}} Following the season, he hired an agent and declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]]{{cite news|last1=Peterson|first1=Randy|title=Wigginton, Horton-Tucker's NBA Draft choices a product of high-end recruiting|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/randy-peterson/2019/04/04/lindell-wigginton-nba-draft-iowa-state-cyclones-basketball-steve-prohm-talen-horton-tucker/3339920002/|accessdate=5 April 2019|work=Des Moines Register|date=4 April 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Iowa Wolves (2019–2020)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Wigginton joined the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/halifax/2019/06/28/its-official-lindell-wigginton-one-of-three-canadians-named-to-toronto-raptors-summer-league-roster.html|title=Nova Scotia's Lindell Wigginton officially makes Toronto Raptors' Summer League roster|work=Toronto Star|date=28 June 2019|accessdate=2019-07-04}} On September 4, 2019, Wigginton signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN LINDELL WIGGINTON|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-lindell-wigginton|website=NBA.com|accessdate=September 4, 2019|date=September 4, 2019}} Under the deal, he ultimately landed with the Timberwolves’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite news |last1=Lawhon |first1=Danny |title=New energy and a familiar face bring Iowa Wolves into 2019-20 NBA G League season |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/basketball/iowa-wolves/2019/11/07/iowa-wolves-nba-g-league-lindell-wigginton-keita-bates-diop-minnesota-timberwolves/2519525001/ |accessdate=November 26, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=November 7, 2019}} On November 8, he tallied 24 points, seven assists, and six rebounds off the bench in a loss to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite news |title=Lindell Wigginton: Scores 24 off bench in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lindell-wigginton-scores-24-off-bench-in-loss/ |accessdate=February 7, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=November 9, 2019}} Wigginton averaged 15.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game in the G League.{{cite web|title=Explosive Honey Badgers Fuel Offense With Wigginton Signing|url=https://www.cebl.ca/explosive-honey-badgers-fuel-offense-with-wigginton-signing|website=CEBL.com|accessdate=June 14, 2021|date=June 14, 2021}} ===Ironi Nes Ziona (2020)=== On May 18, 2020, Wigginton signed with [[Ironi Nes Ziona B.C.|Ironi Nes Ziona]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]]{{cite news|title=Lindell Wigginton joins Ironi Nes-Ziona|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lindell-wigginton-joins-ironi-nes-ziona/|newspaper=Sportando|accessdate=May 19, 2020|date=May 18, 2020}} where he averaged 8.6 points while shooting .550 from the field. ===Return to Iowa (2021)=== On January 25, 2021, Wigginton re-signed with the Iowa Wolves.{{cite web|first=Randi|last=Burrell|title=Wolves Announce 2021 Roster|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-announce-2021-roster/|website=NBA.com|accessdate=June 14, 2021|date=January 25, 2021}} In 17 games, he averaged 17.1 points, 5.2 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 34.9 minutes while shooting .549 from the field. ===Hamilton Honey Badgers (2021)=== On June 14, 2021, Wigginton signed with the [[Hamilton Honey Badgers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]]. ===Wisconsin Herd (2021–2022)=== In October 2021, Wigginton joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]] after being acquired in a trade.{{cite web |title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2021 Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2021-training-camp-roster/n-5758540 |website=Our Sports Central |access-date=October 31, 2021 |date=October 26, 2021}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2022)=== On January 13, 2022, Wigginton signed a two-way contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Lindell Wigginton To A Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-lindell-wigginton-two-way-contract|access-date=January 13, 2022|website=NBA}} On April 10, Wigginton scored 18 points and recorded 8 assists during Milwaukee's final regular season game, a loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].[https://www.cbssports.com/nba/gametracker/tweets/NBA_20220410_MIL@CLE/ Cavs blast Bucks backups 133-115 to earn No. 8 play-in seed] On July 8, 2022, Wigginton re-signed with the Bucks.{{Cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks re-sign Lindell Wigginton |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-re-sign-lindell-wigginton |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} Wigginton joined the Bucks' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster. In his Summer League debut for the Bucks, Wigginton scored seventeen points and seven assists in a 94–90 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets vs Milwaukee Bucks Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/bkn-vs-mil-1522200006/box-score#box-score |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.nba.com}} On July 18, 2022, Wigginton was named to the All-NBA Summer League Second Team.{{Cite web |date=2022-07-18 |title=Lindell Wigginton named to NBA all-Summer League second team |url=https://cyclonefanatic.com/2022/07/lindell-wigginton-named-to-nba-all-summer-league-second-team/ |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=CycloneFanatic.com |language=en-US}} ===Return to Wisconsin (2022–2023)=== On November 3, 2022, Wigginton was named to the opening night roster for the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2022-23-opening-day-roster/n-5895537|title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2022-23 Opening Day Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} ===Return to the Bucks (2023–2024)=== On March 7, 2023, Wigginton signed a two-way contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Lindell Wigginton To A Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-lindell-wigginton-to-a-two-way-contract-2|website=NBA.com|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}} On January 7, 2024, he was waived by the Bucks.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Request Waivers on Marques Bolden and Lindell Wigginton|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-request-waivers-on-marques-bolden-and-lindell-wigginton-2|website=NBA.com|date=January 7, 2024|access-date=January 7, 2024}} ===Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2024)=== On February 5, 2024, Wigginton signed with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web|title=Flying Tigers land Lindell Wigginton|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/852085/Flying-Tigers-land-Lindell-Wigginton|website=Asia-Basket.com|date=February 5, 2024|access-date=February 5, 2024}} ===Shandong Hi-Speed Kirin (2024)=== On August 24, 2024, Wigginton signed with [[Shandong Hi-Speed Kirin]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web|title=【官方公告】|url=https://weibo.com/5167501876/OtSB0udwh?pagetype=profilefeed|website=Weibo.com|publisher=[[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]]|date=August 24, 2024|access-date=August 25, 2024|language=Chinese}} ==National team career== In 2016, Wigginton helped lead Team Canada to a silver medal at the [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]] in [[Valdivia]], [[Chile]]{{Cite news|url=http://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Lindell_Wigginton/B12/Iowa-State-University/385759|title=Lindell Wigginton Basketball Player Profile, High School, News, Career, Awards - usbasket|work=www.eurobasket.com|access-date=2017-07-10}} and played a crucial role in Canada's run to gold at the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2017 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Cairo]], [[Egypt]], as he averaged 12.4 points, 7.0 rebounds and 4.2 assists per game during the tournament. He missed the quarter and semi final due to concussive symptoms,{{Cite news|url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2017/07/07/lindell-wigginton-out-canada-basketball-today-concussion-symptoms/459797001/|title=Lindell Wigginton out for Canada basketball with concussive symptoms|work=Des Moines Register|access-date=2017-07-10|language=en}} but was back for the championship game against [[Italy]], scoring eleven points while tallying three rebounds and three assists.{{Cite web|url=https://fiba.com/world/u19/2017/Italy|title=Italy at the FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2017 - FIBA.basketball|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=2017-07-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170710052959/http://www.fiba.com/world/u19/2017/Italy|archive-date=2017-07-10|url-status=dead}}
